title: The Secret Garden Expedition
clue: Behind a gate you have passed a hundred times is somewhere you have never been.
reveal: Seek out a dog-welcoming garden you have never visited and give it three stops, each with its own sense: your eyes at the gate, your ears in the heart, and your dog's nose in the hidden corner.
objective: Visit a new dog-welcoming garden and make three stops: a Gate for your eyes, a Heart for your ears and a Hidden Corner for your dog's nose.
instructions: Choose a garden or green space you have never entered: a community garden, pocket park, botanic garden or churchyard path. Check its website or phone to confirm dogs are allowed, leash rules and any entry fee.
Take a leash, water, waste bags and, if you like, a small notebook. Go at a quiet time, such as a weekday morning.
Stop 1, the Gate: stand at the entrance for a minute and look. What color is the first thing you see? Let your dog sniff the entrance on a loose leash.
Stop 2, the Heart: wander until your dog's route leads to the middle of the garden. Close your eyes for a minute and listen: water, birds, wind, leaves. Name the best sound.

Stop 3, the Hidden Corner: find the quietest, least-used corner. Let your dog sniff as long as they like on a clear path edge, away from mulch, mushrooms, plants and ponds, and see which smell is worth most of their time.
Keep your dog away from flowerbeds, mulch, mushrooms and pond edges, and do not pick or collect anything. Rest on a bench with water.
On the way out, say your three notes aloud: the color, the sound, the sniff. That is the garden's entry in your passport.
twist: Each stop belongs to a sense: you read the Gate with your eyes, the Heart with your ears and the Hidden Corner with your nose, led by your dog.
variations: Garden center version: visit a dog-welcoming garden center in a quiet hour; before buying a plant for home, check its name on the ASPCA toxic and non-toxic plant list.
Easier: a garden with level paths and benches, with only the Gate and Heart stops.
Seated version: sit on a bench at the Heart and let your dog explore the leash length.
Quieter version: go first thing in the morning and skip the Hidden Corner if it is busy.
completion: You have made your three stops in a new garden at your dog's pace, and left everything as you found it.
photoIdea: Your dog at the Hidden Corner, photographed from the side with the planting behind them.
memoryPrompt: Which color, sound and smell did you choose, and which did your dog care about most?
substitutes: Phone notes instead of a notebook

reservation.note: Nothing to book, but confirm the garden allows dogs, its leash rules and any entry fee, as many gardens do not.

safety: Confirm dogs are allowed and keep yours leashed; no sniffing of mulch, mushrooms, bait or pond edges.
Many garden plants are toxic to dogs, so keep them from eating plants and check any plant names on the ASPCA lists.
Watch for bees, slippery paths and warm paving; skip hot days and leave if it gets busy.
